I ran across this by accident when installing a 2nd hdd in a dell laptop. Windows stores its downloaded updates in a phantom partition using designation "D:\" to break this process.

NOTE: IF YOU CALL TECH SUPPORT FOR ANY HELP WITH COMPUTERS, DO NOT FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS. IT COULD BREAK YOUR COMPUTER!

open Disk Management. it is found by right clicking on the start menu.

locate C:\

right click on the box, then click on shrink Volume.

after menu loads, it will ask you for how much to shrink the volume by, I have 1TB HDD, i shrunk the partition by 100GB. (this is where you could break your computer. never shrink the HDD smaller than currently used space +50% if you plan on never adding anything to it again. windows 10 needs ~25% free space to not chug in click response time. I prefer to dedicate 100GB to each OS on my computers for peace of mind.)

right click on "unallocated ", New simple volume

follow menu to its conclusion, watching for drive letter assignment, set that to "D:\"

part B

Set your connection as a "Metered Connection"

Verification is to run windows update and receive an error when attempting to install an update.

Benefits happen when you read about yet another feature windows 10 broke in an update, while your un updated computer still works.

As of yesterday, i now receive errors that updates can not be downloaded. Feels soo good!
PSA: how to break windows 10 updates with Disk management

Another method is to set your connection as a "metered connection" (mentioned in your post) so that Windows will check for updates but will ask your permission before downloading anything. Unfortunately you can only set a wireless connection as metered, but you can make one quick registry change to manually set a wired connection as a "metered connection", instructions below:

  • Meter your Ethernet connection in Windows 10 :: CNET :: Archive

Edit: it also occurred to me that this isn't strictly gaming. I'm not going to remove it, but you might also consider cross-posting to /v/Technology to make sure they're included.

Or go to services.msc and disable Windows Update. Yeah, I know - black magic.

Since I've disabled it on W10 Pro, it has never prompted for an update, displayed warnings, or in any way annoyed me about it. Last update I graciously allowed it to install was KB3163018, on 16-06-2016. Other than that I've blocked known M$ addresses in external firewall, so even if it silently tries to ping for help, it won't go past it.
